caption:
Swipe through. GPT-6 Astra is live. Sam Altman thanked paying users for their patience while most of them still can't open it 👀

GPT-6 Astra went live on September 4, 2026, Pro and Enterprise and Business Premium got access immediately, API access opened to developers the same moment, Plus and Business users are next but still waiting, Sam Altman announced it in a four-sentence post on X, the post reached 1.9 million views, the post thanked paying users for their patience while most of them were still locked out.

OpenAI is separating the people building products from the people using them, faster than anyone expected. The gap between what developers can ship with GPT-6 today and what regular users can even try is already here.
Running a business? DM us 'AI' and we'll show you what GPT-6 could do for yours.

Sources: Sam Altman on X, September 4, 2026

#ChatGPT #GPT6 #OpenAI #ArtificialIntelligence #AINews
pinned_comment: Is 'thank you for the patience' the smoothest CEO move of the year or the bluntest thing a paying customer has ever read? Either way, most of you read it from the waiting room.

candidates: SAM ALTMAN PUBLICLY THANKED CHATGPT USERS FOR THEIR PATIENCE WHILE THEY WERE STILL LOCKED OUT OF GPT-6 ASTRA
SAM ALTMAN DROPPED GPT-6 ASTRA FOR TOP SUBSCRIBERS AND TOLD EVERYONE ELSE THANK YOU FOR THE PATIENCE
hook_tournament.why: [1] hits harder because it makes the class divide immediate and personal. [0] wraps the same facts in contradiction that requires a mental beat to parse, slowing the emotional punch.

candidates: SAM ALTMAN JUST GAVE CHATGPT'S GPT-6 TO PRO USERS AND IF YOU'RE ON PLUS, YOU'RE STILL WAITING
SAM ALTMAN JUST LAUNCHED CHATGPT'S GPT-6 AND MOST PAYING SUBSCRIBERS STILL CAN'T TOUCH IT
SAM ALTMAN DROPPED GPT-6 ASTRA FOR TOP SUBSCRIBERS AND TOLD EVERYONE ELSE THANK YOU FOR THE PATIENCE
SAM ALTMAN JUST RELEASED CHATGPT'S GPT-6 AND TOLD MOST PAYING USERS 'THANK YOU FOR THE PATIENCE'
hook_sharpen.why: [2]'s 'DROPPED...TOLD EVERYONE ELSE THANK YOU FOR THE PATIENCE' lands like a real person's infuriated hot take with casual language, capturing the full tone-deaf irony in one arc that makes you stop. [3] has the same story but the quotes make it read formal and journalistic, which kills the outrage energy at 2am scrolling.
